clue.text: Twist a lip on a musical instrument

indicators.note: to twist words is to wrench them out of shape, so the letters of the next three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone contorts their mouth while playing an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' rearranges A LIP ON into PIANOL; the final A is added as it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A player piano, worked by perforated paper rolls, is a mechanical keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Show your years — breathe heavily when put out?

indicators.note: a word put out is stretched open, so the panting word is extended to hold the years

parts.note: to pant is to breathe heavily
the number of your years is your age

explanation.surface: Reveal how old you are and puff hard when you are annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like 'annoyed' but here means stretched out: PANT opens to hold AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand public procession or spectacle is a display put on for an audience.

clue.text: Smart set off to read about the business of war

indicators.note: set off means arranged differently, so the letters of the word before are reordered
about here means turned around, so the letters of the word before it are shuffled

explanation.surface: A fashionable crowd heads off to study military commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart set' looks like one phrase (the fashionable crowd), but 'set off' rearranges SMART into ARMST, and 'about' rearranges READ into RADE.
explanation.definitionFit: The international buying and selling of weapons is commerce that supplies warfare.

clue.text: Nothing sour for the nose to detect

parts.note: nothing is zero, written as the letter O
sour, meaning sullen or grim, is dour

explanation.surface: A smell so faint that nothing sour reaches the nostrils.
explanation.definitionFit: A smell is exactly what a nose picks up.

clue.text: In Syria once, pop drunk after beer

indicators.note: after places the jumbled word behind the beer in the answer

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

indicators.note: drunk means reeling, so the letters of the word next to it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Somewhere in old Syria, a fizzy drink is downed after a beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like the past participle of drink, but it signals the anagram; 'after' puts the scrambled pop behind the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient city of northern Syria, settled for thousands of years.

clue.text: Sold one damaged to some fools

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trader sold faulty goods to a bunch of gullible people.
explanation.definitionFit: A noodle is an informal word for a silly person, so the plural means several simpletons.

clue.text: Born, then died smaller, for no good reason

parts.note: née, the French for born, is used before a woman's maiden name
D is the standard abbreviation for died in records and family trees
smaller in amount is less

explanation.surface: A life summary: born, then died having shrunk, all pointlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done without need is unnecessary, lacking any justification.

clue.text: Wiping out of this primate makes aunt groan

indicators.note: wiping out the order of the ape's name, scrambling it, gives the two later words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Exterminating this ape leaves an elderly relative moaning.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: scrambling the answer gives AUNT GROAN, so rearrange those nine letters to find it.
explanation.definitionFit: A great ape of Borneo and Sumatra with long reddish hair.

clue.text: Ring up about one, for the tree

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the ring word is placed round the one
in a down clue, up means the whole result is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Phone again about something, all for the sake of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside CALL to make CALIL; 'up' turns that round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub or small tree grown for its fragrant purple or white flowers.

clue.text: These joints of meat go off aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard means on a ship, so the spoiling word sits inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS, steamship, is a common abbreviation for a ship
eggs or food that addle go bad, so to go off is to addle

explanation.surface: The ship's meat supply is spoiling on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' reads as setting sail, but it means spoil, as food does; 'aboard' sets that word inside the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of lamb or mutton comprising both loins together, sold as a roasting joint.

clue.text: Hunted creatures around the swamp are yellow

indicators.note: around means the hunted animals surround the marsh word

parts.note: animals hunted for sport are game
a swamp is a bog

explanation.surface: Quarry gathered round the marshland have a golden hue.
explanation.walkthrough: Gamboge is a gum resin used as a golden pigment; 'around' puts the hunted animals round the marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A gum resin used as a deep golden pigment, and the colour named after it.

clue.text: The French media communicated in this way?

definitions.text: The French media communicated in this way?

indicators.note: the question suggests these letters are sent out rearranged, so the French article and the media word are shuffled together

parts.note: le is the French for the

explanation.surface: A question about how the French press passes on its news.
explanation.walkthrough: LE plus MEDIA, rearranged, gives the answer, which is also how modern media might send messages.
explanation.definitionFit: Sent electronically over the internet as a message.

clue.text: Just the man to harp on about what's reasonable, in the event!

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters of the phrase before it are rearranged

parts.note: reasonable, following sound reasoning, means logical

explanation.surface: This is exactly the person to keep banging on about sensible matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harp on' looks like nagging, but 'about' scrambles those letters. 'Just the man' is a loose definition: concerned only with humankind, the subject of anthropology.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the study of humankind and human societies.

clue.text: Roofing needed for church as indicated ahead

indicators.note: ahead tells you the pointing word goes in front of the church letters

parts.note: that, used when pointing something out, is the word for what is indicated

explanation.surface: A church needs roofing work, as the sign shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw or reeds laid as a roof covering on cottages.

clue.text: Craftsman made fish come inside

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
to come inside is to enter

explanation.surface: A craftsman cooked fish and then invited it indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworker who makes and repairs wooden structures.

clue.text: Set out to collect the remains

definitions.text: Set out to collect the remains

parts.words: Set out to collect the remains
parts.note: reads like mourners gathering a body or ashes, but describes small dishes laid on tables to catch what is left of cigarettes

explanation.surface: Mourners go out to gather a loved one's remains.
explanation.walkthrough: The remains are cigarette ash, not a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishes put out to receive cigarette ash and butts.

clue.text: How curate felt when egg varied peculiarly?

indicators.note: peculiarly means in an odd fashion, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A curate's reaction to an unevenly cooked egg.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'curate's egg', a British idiom, is something good in parts; a curate given a dubious egg might feel hard done by.
explanation.definitionFit: Resentful at unfair treatment, as one wronged would feel.

clue.text: Walks this way, bearing officer's stick at the front?

indicators.note: at the front puts the stick word ahead of the bearing letter

parts.note: a swagger stick is the short cane carried by a military officer
a compass bearing such as south is written S

explanation.surface: An officer struts along holding his cane out in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' looks like 'carrying', but it is a compass bearing, S; 'this way' points back to the stick's name, which also describes a strutting walk.
explanation.definitionFit: To strut is to walk with an arrogant, self-important gait.

clue.text: Arches either side of a bridge

definitions.text: Arches either side of a bridge

parts.words: Arches either side of a bridge
parts.note: suggests stone spans of a river crossing, but the bridge is that of the nose and the arches are the curved lines of hair above the eyes

explanation.surface: An engineer describes the spans at each end of a river crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge is the bridge of the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: The arched strips of hair growing above each eye.

clue.text: The Spanish version, metre around its trunk?

definitions.text: The Spanish version, metre around its trunk?

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the

indicators.note: a version is a different rendering, so the letters of the word after it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Spanish account of a tree with a girth of one metre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' signals the anagram, as a fresh rendering of the word; the whole clue then pictures a tree whose trunk measures a metre round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall deciduous tree with serrated leaves, once common in English hedgerows.

clue.text: A leading singer for the opera needed? Nine go around

definitions.text: A leading singer for the opera

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: An opera house needs a lead singer; nine people try out for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene ___ is Tchaikovsky's opera, and its title character is the baritone lead.
explanation.definitionFit: The title role of Tchaikovsky's opera, sung by the principal baritone.

clue.text: Grain that is redistributed here in Africa

indicators.note: redistributed means shared out again in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ie, from Latin id est, is the abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: Surplus grain is shared out again in an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redistributed' rearranges GRAIN plus IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A West African country, the continent's most populous nation.

clue.text: A small amount, for dessert

explanation.surface: Just a little helping of pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny quantity is a trivial bit; also a British pudding of sponge, fruit, custard and cream in layers.

clue.text: Trend-making gear restyled for a growing venture?

indicators.note: restyled means given a new form, so the letters of the three words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fashionable equipment is redesigned for a new business enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing' looks like expanding, but it means raising crops: commercial vegetable and fruit production.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising vegetables and fruit commercially on a smallholding for sale.

clue.text: Ringleader brings into play variety of tricks

parts.note: the leader, or first letter, of the word ring is R
to bring something into play is to use it

explanation.surface: A gang boss deploys a range of dirty tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringleader' is split: the leading letter of 'ring'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruses are wily stratagems, several cunning deceptions.

clue.text: Terminal heart trouble

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so the letters of the word after it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fatal cardiac problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terminal' looks like 'fatal' but is the noun: an electrical connection to ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical connection to the ground, as on a plug, is a grounding terminal.

clue.text: Prize collection of ribbons

explanation.surface: An award made of gathered ribbons.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbon badge awarded as a prize at shows; and literally a rose-shaped gathering of ribbon.

clue.text: Passion to hoard gold till doomsday

indicators.note: to hoard is to store away, so the passion word holds the gold inside it

parts.note: a fever is a state of intense passion or excitement
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Greed drives someone to stockpile gold until the end of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passion' wants to be the definition, but it is the fever; 'to hoard' puts the heraldic gold inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting for all time, until the end of the world.

clue.text: Warrant measures involving twenty two down

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure of width, half an em

indicators.note: involving here means entangling, so the letters of the cross-referenced word are mixed up

parts.note: the clue points to the answer of 22-down, tricks

explanation.surface: A warrant sets out measures that involve a few tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' mixes up RUSES into SURES. The setter seems to have meant 'Warrants measure': as printed, plural 'measures' should give ENS, not EN.
explanation.definitionFit: To guarantee or make certain is to vouch for something.

clue.text: Creature with spines can hide up the creek

indicators.note: up the creek means in a mess, so the letters of the two words before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A prickly animal can conceal itself along the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up the creek' looks like a location but signals an anagram of CAN HIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiny anteater, an egg-laying mammal of Australia and New Guinea.
